verdict: Hilton's fee machine kept humming: revenue rose 7% to $3.3 billion and net income jumped 27% to $536 million, powered by a 5.8% rise in revenue per room and 6% growth in its hotel count.

segments.name: Franchise & licensing fees
segments.note: Fees hotel owners pay to use Hilton's brands and booking system — Hilton's highest-margin money.

segments.name: Management fees
segments.note: Base fees ($96M) plus incentive fees ($71M) for running hotels owned by others.

segments.name: Ownership
segments.note: Revenue from the few hotels Hilton actually owns — down 6% as owned-hotel results softened.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Smaller revenue lines, including co-brand credit card and other fees.

segments.name: Cost reimbursement revenues
segments.note: Money passed through from hotel owners to cover the staff and costs Hilton manages on their behalf — it comes in and goes almost straight back out.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear-and-tear cost of Hilton's buildings, systems and intangibles.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Head office, technology and staff costs of running the Hilton system.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Smaller operating costs that do not fit the other lines.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $184M and a $7M foreign-currency loss, partly offset by $4M of other income — net −$187M.

takeaways.title: Rooms earned more
takeaways.text: System-wide revenue per available room (RevPAR) rose 5.8% currency-neutral, led by the U.S. at +7.0% — guests paid more and filled more rooms.

takeaways.title: The pipeline keeps growing
takeaways.text: Hilton approved 30,500 more rooms for development, taking the pipeline to 543,100 rooms (+5% YoY), and added a net 23,000 rooms in the quarter — net unit growth of 6.0%. Future fee income is being built now.

takeaways.title: Shareholders got paid
takeaways.text: Hilton returned $879 million in the quarter through buybacks (2.6 million shares) and dividends, and expects about $3.5 billion of capital return for the full year.

oneTimers: Hilton announced on October 20, 2026 that it will move its stock listing to Nasdaq (same ticker, HLT) effective November 5, 2026 — a listing change only, with no effect on the numbers.
